words.gloss: basti (medicated enema); kalpa (formulary, set of preparations)

hindi: अब इसलिए हम बस्तिकल्प की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall explain the Basti-kalpa (the preparations for basti, the medicated enema).
notes: Chapter-opening formula; the chapter title is Basti-kalpa. basti = medicated enema (standard); kalpa = formulary, set of preparations. The printed ḻ/ळ in later units (line 05.04.2 'baḻāṃ') is the Marathi-print form of l and is normalised to l in `w` (recorded once, here and in line 05.04.2).

lines_deva: बळां गुडूचीं त्रिफलां सरास्नां द्विपंचमूलं च पलोन्मितानि
lines_iast: baḻāṃ guḍūcīṃ triphalāṃ sarāsnāṃ dvipaṃcamūlaṃ ca palonmitāni

words.gloss: triphalā (the three myrobalans: harītakī, bibhītaka, āmalaka; standard group)
together with; rāsnā (disputed: Pluchea lanceolata or Alpinia galanga, galangal)
two; five; root(s); the ten-root group (dvipañcamūla, also called daśamūla; standard group of ten roots)

words.gram: tat-puruṣa, ppp. ud-√mā, n. nom./acc. pl.

words.gloss: half; tulā (a large unit of weight)

hindi: बला यानी बरियार, गिलोय, त्रिफला यानी हरड़ बहेड़ा और आँवला, रास्ना यानी सम्भवतः रासना या कुलंजन, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, के साथ, और द्विपंचमूल यानी दशमूल, पल से मापे हुए। आठ फल और आधा तुला बकरे का मांस जल में पकाए, चौथाई शेष रखते हुए।
english: Balā (country mallow), guḍūcī (giloy), triphalā (the three myrobalans) together with rāsnā (identity disputed), and the ten-root group (dvipañcamūla), measured by the pala (a unit of weight). Eight fruits, and half a tulā (a unit of weight) of goat meat, one should cook in water, with a quarter remaining.
notes:
line 05.04.2: Start of a recipe that runs on through the next units (GROUPING: lines 05.04.2-6 form one sentence; the verb 'pacet' is in line 05.04.3). The printed ḻ in 'baḻāṃ' is the Marathi-print l (normalised to l). The text names the group dvipañcamūla but does not list its ten roots here. 'palonmitāni' is neuter plural and so does not agree in gender with the feminine nouns; read as 'each measured by the pala'. dvipañcamūla = daśamūla (standard group): the greater five bilva, agnimantha, śyonāka, pāṭalā, gambhārī, and the lesser five śālaparṇī, pṛśniparṇī, bṛhatī, kaṇṭakārī, gokṣura. The text itself does not list them; individual identities of some members are disputed.
OPEN (05.04.2) [minor] gram / sa-rāsnām: bahuvrīhi label on a word that only means 'together with rāsnā' is doubtful (an adverbial/adjectival use qualifying the list); not certain. Suggested: Owner may relabel as 'adj., f. acc. sg.'
line 05.04.3: GROUPING: the sentence continues from line 05.04.2; the drugs of line 05.04.2 are understood as also cooked. Which eight fruits are meant is not stated (not identified here). 'māṃsāt chāgāt' is ablative; read as 'from goat meat', i.e. half a tulā of it. 'caturthaśeṣam' read as 'with a fourth part remaining'.
OPEN (05.04.3) [minor] notes / phalāni: Observation only: the 'eight fruits' are unnamed in the text; keep unidentified (the draft does this correctly). Suggested: none

words.gloss: yavānī (ajwain, Trachyspermum ammi; standard); fruit (the ajwain 'seed' is botanically a fruit)
kuṣṭha (drug name: costus root, Saussurea costus; standard)
ghana (drug name; as a drug usually mustā, nut-grass, Cyperus rotundus; probable; lit. 'dense, cloud')
mṛdvīkā (grape or raisin, Vitis vinifera; standard); kṣaudra (honey; standard); ghṛta (ghee)

hindi: छान लेने पर, यवानीफल यानी अजवायन का फल, बिल्व यानी बेल, कुष्ठ यानी कूठ, वचा यानी बच, शताह्वा यानी सम्भवतः सोआ, घन यानी सम्भवतः नागरमोथा और पिप्पली यानी पीपर के कल्कों से, मृद्वीका यानी मुनक्का या अंगूर, शहद और घी से, तेल के साथ युक्त, सुखोष्ण, और नमक से युक्त।
english: When strained, of yavānī-phala (ajwain fruit), bilva (bael), kuṣṭha (costus root), vacā (sweet flag), śatāhvā (probably dill), ghana (probably nut-grass) and pippalī (long pepper) — Joined with pastes, with mṛdvīkā (grape or raisin), honey (kṣaudra) and ghee, together with oil, pleasantly warm, and endowed with salt.

text_flags.why: possible: 'śatāvhā' has the letters v and h transposed; śatāhvā (dill) is the usual form

notes:
line 05.04.4: GROUPING: the genitive list is completed by 'kalkaiḥ' (with pastes) at the start of line 05.04.5; the translation ends with a dash. 'yavānīphala' is read as one member 'fruit of yavānī'; it could also be two items, yavānī and phala (fruit). 'ghana' is a drug-name use of the word; it is usually explained as mustā but this is probable only (also compare line 05.04.12). 'pūte' is a locative absolute with no noun stated.
line 05.04.5: GROUPING: completes the sentence begun in line 05.04.4 ('when strained, ... with pastes ...'); the subject is understood and not named. 'taila' is oil of an unstated kind. The pastes are probably those of the drugs listed in line 05.04.4 (not stated).

lines_deva: बस्तिः परं सर्वगदप्रमाथी स्वस्थे हितो जीवनबृंहणश्च
बस्तौ च यस्मिन् प्रणितो न कल्कः सर्वत्र दद्यादमुमेव तत्र
lines_iast: bastiḥ paraṃ sarvagadapramāthī svasthe hito jīvanabṛṃhaṇaśca
bastau ca yasmin praṇito na kalkaḥ sarvatra dadyādamumeva tatra
hindi: बस्ति सब गदों यानी रोगों का उत्कृष्ट रूप से नाश करने वाली है, स्वस्थ के लिए हितकर है, और जीवन देने वाली तथा पुष्टि करने वाली है। और जिस बस्ति में कल्क नहीं डाला गया हो, उसमें सर्वत्र इसी को दे।
english: The basti is supremely a destroyer of all diseases (gada), beneficial for a healthy person, and life-giving and nourishing (bṛṃhaṇa). And in whichever basti no paste has been introduced, in every case one should give this very one there.
notes:
line 05.04.6: 'jīvanabṛṃhaṇaḥ' can also be read as two qualities, 'jīvana' (life-sustaining) and 'bṛṃhaṇa' (nourishing); both readings give the same sense. The edition's lines all end in a double danda, so no claim is made about how this unit pairs with its neighbours.
line 05.04.7: 'amum' is masculine and is taken to refer to 'kalka' (the paste of lines 05.04.4 and 05.04.5); the text does not say which paste. 'sarvatra' = 'everywhere / in every case'.
OPEN (05.04.7) [minor] english / in every case: 'sarvatra' is 'everywhere'; 'in every case' is an interpretation (the notes already offer it as alternative). Literal rendering preferred. Suggested: everywhere (alternative 'in every case' in notes) - owner choice

words.gloss: two; five; root(s); of the ten-root group (see line 05.04.2)

hindi: दस मूलों के समूह का और अच्छे बकरे के मांस का रस, खट्टे से युक्त, और अनुमान से, छपाई में अस्पष्ट शब्द के अनुसार, पीसने योग्य वस्तु के साथ। तीन स्नेहों से युक्त, श्रेष्ठ निरूह यानी काढ़े की बस्ति, सब अनिल यानी वात की व्याधियों को हरने वाला कहा गया है।
english: The liquid (rasa) of the ten-root group and of good goat meat, joined with something sour (amla), and — on a conjectural reading of the damaged word 'sapairbapeṣyaḥ' — together with what is to be ground. Joined with the three fats (trisneha), the foremost nirūha (decoction enema), declared to be a remover of all diseases of anila (wind, vāta).

text_flags.why: possible: 'sapeṣyaḥ' (with what is to be ground) occurs in unit 23; the printed 'sapairba-' looks like inserted or damaged letters; no firm reading

notes:
line 05.04.8: Damaged word: 'sapairbapeṣyaḥ' is kept unsplit; only its ending '-peṣyaḥ' (to be ground) is recognisable, which is why the translation is marked conjectural. 'sacchāga' is read as sat-chāga 'good goat'; the alternative sa-chāga (with goat) does not suit the genitive. 'amla' = 'sour' (the souring substance is not named). 'rasa' is kept as the Sanskrit word (liquid, juice, broth).
line 05.04.9: The three fats (sneha) are not named in this unit. nirūha = decoction enema (standard modern name). 'anila' = wind = vāta. The edition's lines all end in a double danda, so no claim is made about verse pairing. trisneha is conventionally ghee, oil and animal fat (vasā) or marrow (majjā); standard but the text does not name them here.

lines_deva: प्रस्थो रसाच्छागरसाईयुक्तः साध्यः पुनः प्रस्थसमः स यावत्
lines_iast: prastho rasācchāgarasāīyuktaḥ sādhyaḥ punaḥ prasthasamaḥ sa yāvat

words.gloss: small; five; root(s); the small five-root group (laghupañcamūla; standard group)
trāyantikā (disputed: trāyantī, Gentiana kurroo, or another plant)

hindi: बला यानी बरियार, पटोली यानी परवल, लघुपंचमूल, त्रायन्तिका यानी सम्भवतः त्रायमाण, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, एरण्ड यानी अरंडी और यव से भली-भाँति पकाए हुए से रस में से एक प्रस्थ, बकरे के रस से युक्त, फिर सिद्ध किया जाए जब तक वह एक प्रस्थ के बराबर हो।
english: From what is well cooked of balā, paṭolī (pointed gourd), the small five-root group (laghupañcamūla), trāyantikā (identity disputed), eraṇḍa (castor) and yava (barley) A prastha (a measure) from the liquid (rasa), joined with goat's rasa (broth), is to be prepared again, until it equals a prastha.

text_flags.why: possible: a stray 'ī' after 'rasā'; but the printed line has exactly 22 syllables, so it may instead be a damaged different word; the sense of the whole is not affected

notes:
line 05.04.10: One long compound with an ablative ending on its last member (yava, well-cooked), covering all the drugs. It is taken as 'from (the cooking of) these', with the thing cooked not named; line 05.04.11 continues with 'a prastha from the rasa'. GROUPING: lines 05.04.10-13 form one recipe. The group names laghupañcamūla are not listed in the text. laghupañcamūla (standard group): śālaparṇī, pṛśniparṇī, bṛhatī, kaṇṭakārī, gokṣura; not listed in the text.
line 05.04.11: 'rasāt' is taken as the rasa produced from line 05.04.10. 'yāvat' has no 'tāvat' in the unit; read as 'until it equals a prastha' (cooked down to that measure). 'sādhya' = 'to be prepared'. The stray syllable 'ī' is kept as unclear and left out of the translation.
OPEN (05.04.11) [minor] split / rasācchāgarasāīyuktaḥ: Observation: the stray 'ī' is split off as a word and the rest restored; the 22-syllable count (with ī) means the flag's suggestion 'rasācchāgarasayuktaḥ' gives only 21, so the metre does not support the emendation. A damaged word could instead hide a different reading (e.g. a longer word for 'chāgarasā...'). Translation is not marked conjectural; acceptable for a medium-confidence unit but owner may want 'on a conjectural reading'. Suggested: none

words.gloss: priyaṅgu (disputed: usually Callicarpa macrophylla; other plants also proposed)
kṛṣṇā (long pepper, Piper longum; standard; same as pippalī, line 05.04.4)
ghana (drug name; probably mustā, nut-grass, Cyperus rotundus; probable; see line 05.04.4)
together with; oil; ghee; honey; saindhava (rock salt; standard; lit. 'of Sindhu')

hindi: प्रियंगु यानी सम्भवतः दहिया, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, कृष्णा यानी पीपर और घन यानी सम्भवतः नागरमोथा के कल्क से युक्त, तेल, घी, शहद और सैन्धव यानी सेंधा नमक के साथ। वह दीपन होगा, मांस और बल देने वाला होगा, और आँखों का बल तुरन्त देता है।
english: Joined with a paste of priyaṅgu (identity disputed), kṛṣṇā (long pepper) and ghana (probably nut-grass), together with oil, ghee, honey and saindhava (rock salt). It would be a kindler (dīpana), a giver of flesh and strength, and it at once bestows strength of the eyes.
notes:
line 05.04.12: Continues the recipe of lines 05.04.10 and 05.04.11; the subject is the prepared prastha of line 05.04.11. 'saindhava' kept as the name for rock salt (lit. 'of Sindhu'). 'sa-' is taken to govern all four items (oil, ghee, honey, saindhava).
line 05.04.13: Completes the recipe of lines 05.04.10-12. 'cakṣurbalam' is read as 'strength of the eyes'; it could also be 'the eyes and strength' (cakṣuḥ, balam). dīpana = digestive stimulant (standard sense of the term).

words.gloss: from palāśa (probably flame-of-the-forest tree, Butea monosperma; the word also means 'leaf'; probable)
chinnaruhā (a name of guḍūcī, giloy; standard)

hindi: एरण्ड के मूल से तीन पल, वैसे ही पलाश यानी सम्भवतः ढाक से, एक पल का अंश, लघुपंचमूल। रास्ना, बला यानी बरियार, छिन्नरुहा यानी गिलोय, अश्वगन्धा यानी असगंध, पुनर्नवा यानी सांठी, आरग्वध यानी अमलतास और देवदारु यानी देवदार
english: Three palas from the root of eraṇḍa (castor); likewise from palāśa (probably flame-of-the-forest) a portion of one pala; the small five-root group (laghupañcamūla). Rāsnā, balā, chinnaruhā (giloy), aśvagandhā (winter cherry), punarnavā (hogweed), āragvadha (Indian laburnum) and devadāru (deodar).

text_flags.why: possible: 'ārgavadha' has the letters g and a transposed; āragvadha (Cassia fistula) is the known name (printed correctly as -āragvadha- in unit 34)

notes:
line 05.04.14: New recipe begins (lines 05.04.14-18). Elliptical: no verb here; the drugs are cooked in line 05.04.16 ('vipācayet'). 'palāśa' is either the Butea tree (probable) or 'leaf'; the part used is not stated. 'palāṃśam' read as 'a share of one pala'.
line 05.04.15: A list of drug names continuing the ingredients of line 05.04.14 (no quantities are given for them in the text). It is one dvandva compound; the final member 'devadāru' is neuter.

words.gram: ppp. caus. √śiṣ, n. loc. sg. (loc. abs.)

words.gloss: yaṣṭī (liquorice, Glycyrrhiza glabra; standard; short for yaṣṭīmadhu)
kaṇā (long pepper, Piper longum; standard; same as pippalī, line 05.04.4)
vatsaka (a name of kuṭaja, kurchi, Holarrhena antidysenterica; standard); seed (the seed is called indrayava)

hindi: और आठ फल, दो आढक जल के साथ भली-भाँति पकाए, इसका आठवाँ भाग शेष रहने पर। वचा यानी बच, शताह्वा यानी सम्भवतः सोआ, पुष्पामि जो छपाई में अस्पष्ट है, प्रियंगु जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, यष्टी यानी मुलेठी, कणा यानी पीपर, वत्सक के बीज यानी कुटज के बीज, और मुस्ता यानी नागरमोथा
english: And eight fruits: with two āḍhakas (a measure) of water one should cook thoroughly, with an eighth of this remaining. Vacā (sweet flag), śatāhvā (probably dill), puṣpāmi (unclear in print), priyaṅgu (identity disputed), yaṣṭī (liquorice), kaṇā (long pepper), the seeds of vatsaka (kuṭaja, kurchi) and musta (nut-grass).

text_flags.why: possible: 'śatāvhā' has v and h transposed; śatāhvā is the usual form

notes:
line 05.04.16: The eight fruits are not named here. 'aṣṭamaśeṣite' is a locative absolute, 'this being left at an eighth'; what the eighth is a fraction of is not stated (the water is the natural reading). 'salilāḍhakābhyām' is dual: two āḍhakas of water.
line 05.04.17: Damaged or unclear: 'puṣpāmi' (a flower-word 'puṣpa-' may be meant, but 'āmi' is not recognisable; no firm reading, kept unsplit). The compound is a list of drug names (a paste, see line 05.04.18). 'vatsakabīja' is read as 'seeds of vatsaka'; musta is read as a separate item.
OPEN (05.04.17) [minor] confidence / puṣpāmi: Observation: no 'on a conjectural reading' phrase in the translations, but the damaged word is named as unclear and the rest is a plain list, so acceptable. Suggested: none

words.gloss: tārkṣyaśaila (disputed: commentators explain it as rasāñjana, an extract of Indian barberry)
together with; mākṣika (probably honey; the word also names a mineral, pyrite; probable)

hindi: भली-भाँति पीसकर दे, तार्क्ष्यशैल के साथ जो सम्भवतः रसौत है, अक्ष के माप का, नमक के अंश से युक्त। वह बस्ति, माक्षिक यानी सम्भवतः शहद के साथ, तेल से युक्त, मूत्र के साथ, लेखन और दीपन करने वाली, जीत लेगी
english: One should give it well ground, together with tārkṣyaśaila (possibly rasāñjana, an extract of Indian barberry; disputed), of the measure of an akṣa (a unit of weight), joined with a portion of salt. That basti, with mākṣika (probably honey), joined with oil, with urine, scraping (lekhana) and kindling (dīpana), would overcome —
notes:
line 05.04.18: The object of 'dadyāt' is the list of line 05.04.17, understood and not named. 'saha' takes an accusative here, which is unusual. Identification of tārkṣyaśaila is disputed; the commentators' explanation rasāñjana is only given as a possibility. Whether the akṣa measure belongs to tārkṣyaśaila alone or to the whole is not stated.
OPEN (05.04.18) [minor] gloss / tārkṣya-śailam: Observation, needs owner: tārkṣyaśaila is explained differently by different authorities (rasāñjana is one; a collyrium mineral such as srotoñjana is another). 'disputed' is right and the hedge 'possibly' is present in both languages; do not strengthen it. Suggested: none
line 05.04.19: GROUPING: the sentence continues into lines 05.04.20 and 05.04.21, which give what is overcome. 'mākṣika' is probably honey but can also name a mineral; the text does not say. The kind of urine is not stated. The word order 'bastir jayel lekhanadīpano 'sau' puts 'asau' (that) last.

words.gloss: shank; thigh; foot; trika (the lumbosacral region); back; koṣṭha (belly); heart; guhya (private part); pain
gulma (abdominal lump or mass, standard rendering); aśma (stone); badhma (unclear in print); grahaṇī (chronic diarrhoea with malabsorption, sprue-like; standard rendering); guda (anus); arisen from

hindi: जंघा, ऊरु, पैर, त्रिक, पीठ, कोष्ठ, हृदय और गुह्य अंग की पीड़ा; भारीपन; और विबन्ध यानी मल का रुकना और अनुमान से गुल्म, अश्म, बध्म जो छपाई में अस्पष्ट है, ग्रहणी और गुद से उत्पन्न उन-उन रोगों को, तथा कफ और वात से उत्पन्न रोगों को।
english: Pain in the shanks, thighs, feet, trika (lumbosacral region), back, koṣṭha (belly), heart and private part; heaviness; and obstruction (vibandha, constipation) — and, on a conjectural reading, those various diseases that arise from gulma (abdominal lump), aśma (stone), badhma (unclear in print), grahaṇī (chronic diarrhoea) and the anus (guda), and the diseases born of Kapha and Vāta.

text_flags.why: possible: 'badhma' is not a known word; 'vardhma' (a swelling of the groin or scrotum) is a candidate with the same syllable count; no firm reading

notes:
line 05.04.20: Object of 'jayet' (line 05.04.19). Whether 'śūla' (pain) governs every member of the dvandva is the natural reading but is not certain. 'trika' = the lumbosacral region (standard sense). 'vibandha' = obstruction, usually of stool.
line 05.04.21: Object of 'jayet' (line 05.04.19). 'badhma' is unclear and kept as printed; not translated further. The reading of 'gudotthān' is uncertain: it may govern all the preceding members (as translated) or only 'guda'. 'tān tān ca rogān' = 'and those and those diseases' (various). Modern equivalents given only as the standard renderings of the Sanskrit terms: gulma = abdominal lump, grahaṇī = chronic diarrhoea with malabsorption.

words.gloss: four; in a measure of palas
śatāhvā (see line 05.04.4); curd (dadhi); dāḍima (pomegranate, Punica granatum; standard); sour
